ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Inspect boards. Improve automated optical inspection that finds missing, rotated and wrongly placed parts and bad solder, working alongside our AI agents.

 - Pick reliably. Train and deploy the models that find parts in bins and trays, centre them on the nozzle and catch a clumped or dropped pick.

 - Align precisely. Fiducial detection, calibration and image alignment for placements measured in fractions of a millimetre.

 - Build the data loop. Decide what to capture, build labelling tools, and turn operator verdicts into training data.

 - Go fast. Work with our high-speed cameras and GPU capture pipeline to move vision closer to real time.

 - Measure it. Track accuracy in production, find where errors come from, and prove every change against past results.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You've shipped computer vision into production, beyond a notebook.

 - Strong software engineering in Python, C++ or a comparable language.

 - A mix of classical vision (geometry, calibration, template matching) and deep learning; you know when each is the right tool.

 - Experience with industrial or machine-vision cameras is a bonus.

 - You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

 - You like the physical world: lighting, lenses and parts rotated by 90°.


STACK

 - Vision: OpenCV, PyTorch and Lightning, ONNX Runtime on GPU, libtorch from Haskell

 - Cameras: Basler GigE cameras via pylon, high-speed cameras with GPUDirect capture

 - Services: Python and Haskell, PostgreSQL, Nix and NixOS


PAY
